## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15) is a verse narrative preserved in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The story illustrates the karmic principle that even minor evil deeds can yield immense suffering in subsequent existences [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Although SuttaCentral lists no curated parallels, DharmaNexus detects extensive textual reuse between the *Mattāpetivatthu* and other Pali works, as well as machine-generated alignments with non-Pali corpora [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, the text shares substantial material with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (notably across segments §5.1–34.4) and the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as shared formulaic verse sequences with other narratives in the *Petavatthu* and *Vimānavatthu*, including the *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13, §26.3–31.4), *Nandāpetivatthu* (Pv 16, §26.3–35.1), *Sāriputtattheramātupetivatthu* (Pv 14), and *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33) [DharmaNexus]. Across canonical traditions, DharmaNexus aligns passages automatically with the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100), the Sanskrit *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and Tibetan translations including the *Maitreyaparipṛcchā* (D 85) and the *Samādhirājasūtra* (D 127) [DharmaNexus].
